newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares end touch lower, after day of drift.
newsitem.headline: French shares end touch lower, after day of drift.

text.p: French shares closed lower on Monday, unable to hold late afternoon gains made on the back of Wall Street's strength, traders said.

The CAC index earlier hit a fresh all-time high in the session at 3,044.24, but the market's grip slackened and prices slipped back. Brokers said business was very thin, with summer holidays much in the foreground.
The CAC-40 index down 3.74, or 0.12 percent, at 3,022.2.
CAC-40 July futures 3,024 vs 3,028 at Friday's close.
The broader SBF120 index down 1.08 at 2,058.82
Total volume was a moderate 7.5 billion francs.

LVMH dropped 3.07 percent to 1,579. Chairman Bernard Arnault's counter-offer of a 25 percent instead of 35 holding in his proposed Drinks Co was not likely to win approval from Guinness and GrandMet, a broker said.

The British firms want a merger, while Arnault still wants a demerger, with a big minority stake. "They are still opposites," he said, adding "There is too much hostility out there, the market doesn't like that".
However, LVMH's price was supported by dollar strength against the mark and yen, he added.
Pinault-Printemps-Redoute ended down 1.89 percent at 2,796, after running into profit-taking. Shares in the retailer earlier hit a day high of 2,915 on the back of "good" first half sales figures.
In the auto sector, PSA Peugeot Citroen gained 1.15 percent to 703 as Cheuvreux de Virieu added it to its recommended list.
A broker said investors may have switched out of Renault, down 3.18 percent at 176.4, and Valeo, down 2.48 percent at 381.9, to make room for Peugeot stock.
The bank sector continued to hold some allure, with CCF rising 3.28 percent to 299.5, with a block of 480,000 shares changing hands at 289.80.
Other financials holding potential for gains include and BNP, up 0.76 percent to 280.10, Societe Generale, up 0.64 percent to 790, and Paribas, up 1.48 percent at 432.3.
Lafarge rises 2.17 percent to 418.10, helped by dollar strength agh U.S. subsidiary Lafarge Corp.
The dollar hit a 7-1/2 year high in the afternoon against the mark.

Some brokers estimate the government's plans to backdate a new rate of 41.6 percent company tax to January 1 will hit earnings of CAC 40 companies by between two and three percent, a margin deemed acceptable by the market, a trader said.
